description: IAM policy-evaluation regression corpus. Expected outcomes come from the AWS documentation cited in each case, not from this project's evaluator. Accounts 111111111111 (analyzed) and 222222222222 (other) are synthetic. A null context value means the key is known to be absent from the request; a missing key means its value is unknown. See docs/iam-regression-cases.md.

cases.title: An explicit Deny in an identity policy overrides an Allow in the same identity policy

source.rule: If the enforcement code finds even one explicit Deny that applies to the request, the final decision is Deny regardless of any Allow statements.

cases.title: An explicit Deny in a bucket policy overrides an Allow in the caller's identity policy

source.rule: When identity-based and resource-based policies are evaluated together, an explicit deny in either of them overrides the allow.

cases.title: A request that no statement allows is implicitly denied

source.rule: By default all requests are implicitly denied; a request must be explicitly allowed by an applicable policy to be allowed.

cases.title: s3:Get* in a group policy matches s3:GetObject for a member of the group

source.rule: Wildcards (* and ?) can be used as part of an action name, so s3:Get* applies to every S3 action whose name starts with Get.

simulator.note: Group policies are passed in PolicyInputList together with the user's own policies; the simulator has no notion of group membership.

cases.title: s3:* in an attached managed policy matches any S3 action

source.rule: An Action element of s3:* applies to all S3 actions.

cases.title: Action * with Resource * matches an action of any service

source.rule: The multi-character wildcard * matches any combination of characters in an action name, so a bare * matches every action of every service.

cases.title: S3:GETOBJECT in the policy matches the request action s3:GetObject

source.rule: The service prefix and the action name are case insensitive, so iam:ListAccessKeys is the same as IAM:listaccesskeys.

cases.title: ? matches one character and * expands across slashes in the resource part of an ARN

source.rule: In a resource ARN ? matches any single character and * matches any combination of characters, including the forward slash, within the resource segment.

cases.title: Allow with NotAction iam:* grants an S3 action

source.rule: NotAction matches everything except the listed actions, so with the Allow effect every applicable action that is not listed is allowed.

cases.title: Deny with NotAction s3:GetObject explicitly denies s3:PutObject

source.rule: With the Deny effect, NotAction explicitly denies every action that is not listed while leaving the listed actions unaffected.

cases.title: Allow with NotResource secret/* grants access to an object in another bucket

source.rule: NotResource matches every resource except those specified, so an Allow applies to all resources that are not listed.

cases.title: Deny s3:* with NotResource data explicitly denies objects outside the data bucket

source.rule: Using NotResource with the Deny effect explicitly denies access to every resource that is not listed, without granting the listed ones.

cases.title: Identity policy allows everything but the boundary allows only S3: iam:CreateUser is implicitly denied

source.rule: An entity may perform only the actions allowed by both its identity-based policies and its permissions boundary; a boundary that does not allow the action results in an implicit deny.

cases.title: An explicit Deny in the permissions boundary overrides the identity policy Allow

source.rule: The effective permissions are the intersection of identity-based policies and the boundary, and an explicit deny in either of them overrides the allow.

cases.title: A permissions boundary that allows S3 does not grant S3 access to a user without identity policies

source.rule: A policy used as a permissions boundary limits the user's permissions but does not provide permissions on its own.

cases.title: A same-account bucket policy naming the user ARN grants access without any identity policy

source.rule: Within the same account, resource-based policies that grant permissions to an IAM user ARN are not limited by an implicit deny in an identity-based policy.

cases.title: A same-account identity policy grants access even though the bucket policy names only another user

source.rule: Within the same account the permissions are the union of identity-based and resource-based policies: if an action is allowed by either one, AWS allows the action.

cases.title: A bucket policy in another account naming the user is not enough without an identity policy Allow

source.rule: For a cross-account request the identity-based policy in the trusted account and the resource-based policy in the trusting account must both allow it; the request is allowed only if both evaluations return Allow.

cases.title: An identity policy Allow is not enough when the other account's bucket policy does not grant the caller

source.rule: For a cross-account request the resource-based policy in the trusting account must allow the requester in addition to the identity-based policy in the trusted account.

cases.title: Identity policy Allow plus a bucket policy delegating to the caller's account allows the cross-account request

source.rule: In cross-account access a principal needs an Allow in the identity policy and in the resource-based policy; a resource policy naming the account root delegates access to the account, whose identity policies then grant it.

cases.title: StringEquals matches an exact value and StringEqualsIgnoreCase matches regardless of case

source.rule: StringEquals performs exact, case-sensitive matching and StringEqualsIgnoreCase performs exact matching ignoring case; multiple condition operators are combined with a logical AND.

cases.title: A Deny conditioned on StringNotEquals aws:RequestedRegion applies to a request for another Region

source.rule: StringNotEquals is negated matching: the condition is true when the request value does not equal the policy value.

cases.title: StringLike proj-?lph* matches the principal tag value proj-alpha

source.rule: StringLike is case-sensitive matching whose values can include multi-character (*) and single-character (?) wildcards anywhere in the string.

cases.title: Bool aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent true with NumericLessThanEquals aws:MultiFactorAuthAge 3600 matches a fresh MFA session

source.rule: Bool matches a boolean value and NumericLessThanEquals matches when the request value is less than or equal to the policy value; both operators in one Condition must match.

cases.title: Null aws:TokenIssueTime true matches a request made without temporary credentials

source.rule: The Null condition operator with the value true matches when the condition key does not exist in the request context.

simulator.note: A null context value in the corpus means the key is absent; the validator omits the ContextEntry for it.

cases.title: Null aws:TokenIssueTime false does not match a request made without temporary credentials

source.rule: The Null condition operator with the value false matches only when the key exists in the request context and its value is not null.

simulator.note: A null context value in the corpus means the key is absent; the validator omits the ContextEntry for it.

cases.title: An address inside 203.0.113.0/24 satisfies IpAddress and does not trigger the NotIpAddress Deny

source.rule: IpAddress matches the specified IP address or CIDR range and NotIpAddress matches all addresses except the specified range.

cases.title: DateGreaterThan aws:CurrentTime 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z matches a request made in June 2026

source.rule: DateGreaterThan matches when the request date/time is after the specified date and time (ISO 8601 or epoch values).

cases.title: BoolIfExists aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent false in a Deny applies when the key is absent

source.rule: With an ...IfExists operator the key is processed as specified when present and the condition element evaluates to true when the key is not present.

simulator.note: A null context value in the corpus means the key is absent; the validator omits the ContextEntry for it.

cases.title: ForAllValues:StringEquals matches when every requested tag key is in the policy list

source.rule: ForAllValues returns true if every context key value in the request matches a context key value in the policy.

cases.title: ForAnyValue:StringEquals matches when at least one requested tag key is in the policy list

source.rule: ForAnyValue returns true if any one of the context key values in the request matches any one of the context key values in the policy.

cases.title: A condition on aws:SourceVpce cannot be decided without a request-time value

source.rule: aws:SourceVpce is included in the request context only if the requester uses a VPC endpoint, so the outcome depends on the request: the Allow applies when the key equals the policy value and the request is implicitly denied when the key is absent or different.

simulator.note: The simulator has no indeterminate outcome: without a ContextEntry for aws:SourceVpce it reports implicitDeny and lists the key under MissingContextValues; with a value it reports allowed or implicitDeny. Supply a value to simulate one branch.

cases.title: ForAllValues:StringEquals evaluates to true when the request carries no aws:TagKeys

source.rule: ForAllValues also returns true if there are no context keys in the request, which is why AWS recommends pairing it with a Null false check.

simulator.note: A null context value in the corpus means the key is absent; the validator omits the ContextEntry for it.

cases.title: StringNotEquals aws:SourceVpce in a Deny applies to a request that carries no aws:SourceVpce

source.rule: If the policy condition requires that the key is not matched (StringNotEquals, StringNotLike, ArnNotLike, ...) and the key is not present in the request context, the condition is true.

simulator.note: A null context value in the corpus means the key is absent; the validator omits the ContextEntry for it.

cases.title: ${aws:username} in the Resource element resolves to the calling user's name

source.rule: When the policy is evaluated, policy variables are replaced with values from the request context, so ${aws:username} in a Resource ARN matches only the caller's own prefix.

simulator.note: aws:username is supplied as a ContextEntry from the principal's name so the simulator can resolve the variable.

cases.title: ${aws:PrincipalTag/team} in the Resource element resolves to the caller's team tag

source.rule: ${aws:PrincipalTag/tag-key} is a policy variable that is replaced with the value of the principal's tag when the policy is evaluated.

simulator.note: aws:PrincipalTag/team is supplied as a ContextEntry from the principal's tags so the simulator can resolve the variable.

cases.title: ${aws:username} is a literal string in a policy that has no Version element

source.rule: Policy variables are supported only with Version 2012-10-17; if the Version element is missing or earlier, variables like ${aws:username} are treated as literal strings.

simulator.note: The policy document is passed without a Version element; aws:username is still supplied as a ContextEntry so that any substitution would be observable.

cases.title: ArnLike aws:PrincipalArn arn:aws:iam::111111111111:user/al* matches the calling user

source.rule: aws:PrincipalArn is included in the request context for all signed requests and holds the caller's ARN; ArnLike compares it case-sensitively with * and ? wildcards.

simulator.note: aws:PrincipalArn is supplied as a ContextEntry from the principal ARN; SimulateCustomPolicy has no real caller identity.

cases.title: A bucket policy with Principal * restricted to aws:PrincipalAccount 111111111111 grants a same-account user

source.rule: aws:PrincipalAccount is included in the request context for all requests and holds the caller's account; a resource-based Allow with a wildcard Principal needs no other permissions for IAM users of the same account.

simulator.note: aws:PrincipalAccount is supplied as a ContextEntry from the principal's account in addition to CallerArn.

cases.title: StringEquals aws:SourceAccount does not match a request made directly by a user

source.rule: aws:SourceAccount is included in the request context only when a service principal calls the resource on behalf of a resource; a key that is not present does not match and the condition is false.

simulator.note: A null context value in the corpus means the key is absent; the validator omits the ContextEntry for it.

cases.title: A bucket policy whose Principal is the account root delegates to the account; the user still needs an identity-based allow

source.rule: Naming an AWS account (its root ARN) as the principal delegates authority to the account: the permission reaches the account's IAM identities only through their own identity-based policies, which must allow the action.

simulator.note: CallerArn is the user and ResourceOwner is the same account; the simulator applies the same delegation rule to an account-root principal.
